metadata.note: The PATCO Speedline and the Bridge Line it grew out of. The Delaware River Joint Commission opened a two-station rapid-transit line across the Benjamin Franklin Bridge from Philadelphia to Camden on 7 June 1936 — the 'Bridge Line'. The Port Authority Transit Corporation, a subsidiary of the Delaware River Port Authority, rebuilt and extended it out to Lindenwold over the old Pennsylvania-Reading Seashore Lines right of way, opening the full Speedline in 1969. It was one of the first fully automated rapid-transit lines in the United States and still runs 24 hours a day.
